19.description: The committee recommends reducing the acceptable limit of Total Kjeldahl Nitrogen (TKN) in wastewater to 50 mg/L and adding it to an industrial surcharge program by 2028 to protect the environment and fairly allocate treatment costs.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
4 for, 0 against
Staff explained that ammonia levels increased 65% in the last decade.
All ratepayers currently bear the $726,000 annual cost of TKN removal.
Operating outside permit levels risks fines from the Water Security Agency.
Ammonia discharge can be toxic to fish and alter river ecosystems.
Administration will report back in 2027 with final recommended surcharge rates.

20.description: Saskatoon will explore a free pilot program for air quality sensors to assess localized conditions and identify areas needing green infrastructure.

chips.text: Approved
3 for, 1 against
Staff raised concerns about duplicating provincial air quality monitoring efforts.
Staff stated no identified need for additional air quality monitoring.
Detailed financial information and funding sources for the pilot remain unknown.
Mayor Block opposed, stating the work does not need to be done.
Pilot aims to address equity in air quality for specific neighborhoods.
Sensors measure PM 2.5, PM 10, temperature, and humidity.

21.description: The city's Indigenous Initiatives Department reported on 2025 progress, including increased staff training and community events. It outlined 2026 priorities like a Reconciliation Action Plan and Indigenous cultural spaces.

chips.text: Approved
4 for, 0 against
City Manager offered to report back on the Indigenous apprenticeship program details.
Indigenous businesses received $52,000 in procurement from the department in 2025.
When the Indigenous apprenticeship program's success will be evaluated remains unclear.
Apprenticeship program creates pathways to stable, well-paid jobs for Indigenous individuals.
Staff will review the Indigenous cultural resource position and seek continued funding.

22.description: The Remai Modern art gallery will replace its continuously running boilers, which are failing and obsolete, to ensure regulatory compliance, reduce operational risk, and save approximately $150,000 annually by enabling guarded plant status.

chips.text: Approved
4 for, 0 against
Councillor Davies questioned lessons learned from the Remai Modern's boiler failure.
Taxpayers will save approximately $150,000 annually in operating costs.
Boilers maintain ASHRAE Class AA environmental standards for the facility.
Administration will increase communication and controls for the boiler system.
